newsitem.title: USA: Burlington sees lower Q4 on denim slowdown.
newsitem.headline: Burlington sees lower Q4 on denim slowdown.

text.p: Burlington Industries Inc said Thursday it expects to post earnings for the fourth quarter ending September 28 slightly below the $0.21 per share reported in the 1995 fourth quarter, citing a slowdown in its denim operations.
The textile company said it also expects its fiscal 1997 earnings to come in between $0.20 and $0.30 per share lower than the current consensus of analysts' expectations, about $1.39 per share.
Burlington President and Chief Executive George Henderson said in a statement that the lower projections were the result of its denim operations.
"Excess inventories of denim fabrics have built up in the pipeline, causing us to take selective curtailment in our denim operations," he said.

"While overall demand for denim products remains sound, curtailment while our customers work down their inventories will have a negative effect on our earnings for the current quarter as well as the first half of the 1997 fiscal year," he added.
Analysts' consensus share earnings estimates for Burlington's fourth quarter are $0.28, and for full-year fiscal 1996 the consensus is $1.14.
The company is set to announce its fourth quarter earnings on November 7.
